A tool might warn you if it thinks your title tags are too long or too short, but please note that title tag length is not a ranking factor in Google search as long as you follow title tag best practices.

Item: There are not multiple pages targeting the same keywords.
Where To Check: Manual testing / KW Research (a keyword ranking export in a tool like Semrush can help) / Plugins such as Yoast.
Notes/Reference:
This is all on you however you choose to implement and track it. Plugins like Yoast can help with tracking. Large websites may not be able to avoid some of this, but you should at least ensure your high-priority keywords don't suffer from cannibalization.

Item: Duplicate Content
Site copy is original and not scraped/duplicated from other websites.
Notes/Reference: Remember that when an SEO tool checks for "duplicate content," it might only be checking your internal pages. Make sure you run a plagiarism checker, especially if the website has old blog posts or UGC that you did not have control over.

Item: Make sure HTTP:// site version directs to HTTPS:// version.
Where To Check: Varvy Redirect Mapper, Screaming Frog, Semrush, or another crawling tool that reports on redirects.
Notes/Reference:
Even when your site runs on HTTPS, circumstances like user error can cause devices to try and access an HTTP version. There might be errors in redirecting some pages.
SSL Redirection Guide

Item: Different versions of the same URL (parameters such as UTM codes, trailing slashes, etc.) are treated properly.
Notes/Reference:
Note that Google crawlers are much better at understanding URL paramaters than they used to be, leading to Google deprecating the URL parameters tool in Search Console, so this may not be a critical issue.

Item: Internal Links
Make sure internal links don't have rel=nofollow attribute.
Notes/Reference:
Google: Nofollow Is Not A Substitute For Noindex 
Needing a nofollow tag on an internal link is quite rare. If you want Google not to count an internal link, it's better to noindex the destination page instead.

Item: Internal linking reflects the priority of content.
Notes/Reference:
This has a little bit of overlap with a content audit, which is beyond the scope of this worksheet, but internal linking is good to address here, too. 
Internal Linking Is Super Critical For SEO
Internal Links As A Ranking Factor

Item: Internal links are crawlable and use best practices.
Notes/Reference: Google's documentation on internal links best practices

Item: Important content is ≤4 clicks from the homepage.
Where To Check: Manual testing. You can use your chosen crawling tool to help, but identify the important pages and test how users navigate to them.
Notes/Reference: How To Improve Your Website Navigation: 7 Essential Best Practices

Item: There are fewer than ~300 links on important pages.
Notes/Reference: Neither Google nor Bing state an explicit limit on the number of links, however Google's John Mueller has cautioned that too many internal links can potentially make a website more confusing for Google to interpret. Both Google and Bing suggest that the number of links on a page should make sense, and be "reasonable." That changes depending on the use case for a site/page, but multiple hundreds of links is probably too many.

Item: Structured Data
Structured data doesn't have validation errors.
Where To Check: Google Search Console / Structured Data Testing Tool.
Notes/Reference: How To Test And Validate Structured Data

Item: Schema markup matches the content of the page to avoid being considered misleading/spam.
Notes/Reference: Don't tag your content as something it's not.
